_rule: The verified law every estate build's compliance map is generated from. Each duty quotes its primary text, links it and gives the date checked; appliesIf names the facts (one or all of a list) a build must declare for the duty to apply; status says what each stack (local / cloud / saas) does to it. Shared by every build through comply.mjs; builds pull this file, they never retype it.

aia.name: EU AI Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI, OJ 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026)

ukgdpr.name: UK GDPR, as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 (data protection provisions in force 5 February 2026: SI 2026/82, regulation 2)

dates.what: AI Act Chapters I and II apply — including Article 4 (AI literacy) and the Article 5 prohibitions
UK: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 data protection provisions in force — including section 80 (new Articles 22A–22D on automated decision-making) and section 85 / Schedule 7 (international transfers)
Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) in force
AI Act general date of application — including Article 50 transparency
AI Act Article 50(2) marking for generative systems already on the market before 2 August 2026; and the new Article 5(1) points (ba) and (bb)
dates.ref: Art 111(4) and Art 113, third para, point (a), as amended by Reg 2026/1744

dates.what: AI Act high-risk obligations (Chapter III, Sections 1–3) for Annex III systems — moved from 2 August 2026 by the Digital Omnibus
dates.ref: Art 113, third para, point (c)(i), as replaced by Reg 2026/1744

dates.what: AI Act high-risk obligations for Annex I (product-safety) systems
dates.ref: Art 113, third para, point (c)(ii), as replaced by Reg 2026/1744

duties.title: Prohibited AI practices may not be placed on the market, put into service or used
duties.quote: The following AI practices shall be prohibited:

note.local: Where it runs changes nothing: the practice itself is banned in the EU.
note.cloud: Same.
note.saas: Same.

duties.title: A UK company is in scope when its AI output is used in the EU
duties.quote: providers and deployers of AI systems that have their place of establishment or are located in a third country, where the output produced by the AI system is used in the Union

note.local: Where the model runs does not change scope; who uses the output does.
note.cloud: Same.
note.saas: Same.

duties.title: Building an AI system for your own use makes you its provider
duties.quote: ‘putting into service’ means the supply of an AI system for first use directly to the deployer or for own use in the Union for its intended purpose

note.local: Local-first in-house systems: the company is provider and deployer. Plan for provider duties (for this design: Article 50 and AI literacy; full high-risk duties only if a high-risk use is added).
note.cloud: An AI system the company builds on a cloud model API is still the company's system: provider and deployer.
note.saas: A seat product (Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude): the vendor is the provider of its assistant; the company is the deployer.

duties.title: AI literacy
duties.quote: Providers and deployers of AI systems shall take measures to support the development of AI literacy of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf

note.local: Training plan in the operating model (Phase 0).
note.cloud: Same duty.
note.saas: Same duty.

duties.title: Tell people when they are talking to an AI
duties.quote: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system

note.local: In force now. Applies to a customer-facing assistant; drafts that an agent sends as their own do not interact directly.
note.cloud: Same — a support bot built on an API is the company's system.
note.saas: The vendor designs its own assistant's disclosure.

duties.ref: Art 50(2); Art 111(4) as added by Reg 2026/1744
duties.title: Mark AI-generated audio, image, video or text as artificially generated, in a machine-readable format
duties.quote: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.

note.local: Where the model runs changes nothing: the outputs carry the mark. Systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 have until 2 December 2026 (Art 111(4)). Not required where the system only assists standard editing.
note.cloud: Same.
note.saas: The vendor, as provider, carries the marking duty for its outputs; the company does not strip the mark.

duties.ref: Art 6(2), Annex III; Art 6(3) derogation; Art 113(c)(i)
duties.title: High-risk uses (e.g. creditworthiness, employment decisions) — from 2 December 2027
duties.quote: (b) AI systems intended to be used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons or establish their credit score, with the exception of AI systems used for the purpose of detecting financial fraud

note.local: Full provider duties (risk management, data governance, logging, human oversight, conformity) — the design keeps high-risk uses out of the first rollout.
note.cloud: Same duties; a cloud model does not carry them for you.
note.saas: Same for any high-risk use of the tool.

duties.title: Deployer duties for high-risk systems: human oversight, monitoring, logs kept at least six months
duties.quote: Deployers shall assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority … keep the logs automatically generated by that high-risk AI system … of at least six months

note.local: The signed hop ledger is the log, under the company's control. Financial institutions meet the monitoring and log duties through their financial-services governance (Art 26(5), (6)).
note.cloud: Logs split between the company and the vendor.
note.saas: Logs largely the vendor's.

duties.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment before deploying credit scoring
duties.quote: deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in points 5 (b) and (c) of Annex III, shall perform an assessment of the impact on fundamental rights

note.local: Only if credit scoring is ever added.
note.cloud: Same.
note.saas: Same.

duties.title: Fines
duties.quote: up to EUR 15 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 3 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher

note.local: Up to EUR 35 000 000 or 7 % for prohibited practices (Art 99(3)).
note.cloud: Same.
note.saas: Same.

duties.title: Accuracy, and being able to prove compliance
duties.quote: accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date … The controller shall be responsible for, and be able to demonstrate compliance with, paragraph 1 (‘accountability’)

note.local: Accuracy is yours on every stack (the measured small models were not accurate enough to answer alone). Accountability is easier: every answer has a signed receipt the company holds.
note.cloud: Evidence of what the model did sits partly with the vendor.
note.saas: Evidence sits mostly with the vendor.

duties.title: A lawful basis for each use
duties.quote: Processing shall be lawful only if and to the extent that at least one of the following applies

note.local: Where the model runs does not supply a lawful basis.
note.cloud: Same.
note.saas: Same.

duties.ref: EU Art 22(1); UK Arts 22A–22D (DUAA 2025 s.80, in force 5 Feb 2026)
duties.title: Decisions based solely on automated processing
duties.quote: EU: “the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing … which produces legal effects … or similarly significantly affects him or her”. UK: safeguards must “enable the data subject to obtain human intervention … [and] to contest such decisions” (Art 22C(2))

note.local: The design keeps a person meaningfully in every significant decision.
note.cloud: Same.
note.saas: Same.

duties.title: Data protection by design and by default
duties.quote: the controller shall, both at the time of the determination of the means for processing and at the time of the processing itself, implement appropriate technical and organisational measures

note.local: The strongest minimisation there is: the prompt and the answer never leave the company's machines.
note.cloud: Minimise what is sent; rely on the vendor's retention terms.
note.saas: Rely on the vendor's settings and terms.

duties.title: Processor contracts and due diligence
duties.quote: Where processing is to be carried out on behalf of a controller, the controller shall use only processors providing sufficient guarantees

note.local: No third party processes the prompts or answers, so there is no AI processor to contract, audit or monitor for inference.
note.cloud: The model vendor is a processor: contract, due diligence, sub-processor list, ongoing review.
note.saas: The seat vendor is a processor: the same work.

duties.title: Security of processing
duties.quote: the controller and the processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk

note.local: All of it is in-house: encrypted laptops, the always-on machines that hold the desk and the receipts, access control, the model supply chain (hash-pinned weights).
note.cloud: Split with the vendor under its terms.
note.saas: Split with the vendor under its terms.

duties.ref: Art 35(1); ICO list of high-risk processing
duties.title: Data protection impact assessment
duties.quote: ICO: “Innovative technology: processing involving the use of innovative technologies, or the novel application of existing technologies (including AI). A DPIA is required where this processing is combined with any of the criteria from the European guidelines.”

note.local: Plan a DPIA per workload in Phase 0; the local design removes the transfer and processor risks from it.
note.cloud: Same, plus transfer and processor risks.
note.saas: Same, plus transfer and processor risks.

duties.ref: EU Art 44; UK Chapter V as amended by DUAA 2025 s.85 and Sch 7 (in force 5 Feb 2026)
duties.title: Transfers outside the UK / EEA
duties.quote: Any transfer of personal data which are undergoing processing or are intended for processing after transfer to a third country … shall take place only if … the conditions laid down in this Chapter are complied with

note.local: No personal data leaves the building for inference, so there is no transfer to assess.
note.cloud: If the model runs outside the UK/EEA: an adequacy route or safeguards, and a transfer risk assessment.
note.saas: Same, unless the vendor contracts UK/EU data residency.

duties.ref: ICO, Guidance on AI and data protection (updated 15 March 2023; under review after the DUAA)
duties.title: The UK regulator's AI guidance
duties.quote: Due to changes made by the Data (Use and Access) Act, this guidance is under review and may be subject to change.

note.local: Follow it; watch for the post-DUAA revision.
note.cloud: Same.
note.saas: Same.

duties.title: Personal data in AI model development
duties.quote: Opinion 28/2024 on certain data protection aspects related to the processing of personal data in the context of AI models

note.local: Relevant only if the company fine-tunes models on personal data; this design does not in the first rollout.
note.cloud: Same.
note.saas: Same.
